Level 4 is complete, but it cost 54 actions. The human baseline is 26, so I used about twice as many, below the cap of 130. Most of the extra actions came from finding the rules by trial, plus one game over and a reset.

These are the rules I found:
- **Select, then move:** Click a node (a small ring with a colored center) to select it. It turns black. Then click any cell to move it there. The cell does not have to be inside an outline.
- **Pieces follow their nodes:** Each colored piece sits at the midpoint of its two nodes, or at the center point of its three nodes.
- **Goal:** Put each piece inside the outline with its matching colors. For example, the green-and-blue piece goes into the green-and-blue outline.
- **Danger:** If a piece stops on the large orange area, the game ends. This is what caused my game over.
- **Refused moves:** Some moves did nothing and the node stayed in place. I am not sure why. I guessed that the path was blocked or the target outline was already full.

I saved these rules as a global memory, so a later instance of this game can plan its node positions from the start.
